meta_description: Authorization path rebuilt for latency — p99 down 83% and the peak-season authorization budget met with headroom

blocks.x: Authorization path rebuilt for latency — p99 down 83% and the peak-season authorization budget met with headroom

Identity withheld — a payments platform whose merchants measured it in milliseconds and whose authorization path had accreted nine synchronous hops over seven years. Figures are the client's own, shared with permission.

The baseline trace told the story: p99 authorization at 412ms with merchants' SLAs at 300, peak-season projections exceeding the budget entirely, and each hop owned by a team with a reason it was synchronous.
The reasons were historical — an ordering system here, a fraud pre-check there — and no single view existed of the whole path's latency budget. Every team optimized locally.

We rebuilt the path as a latency budget: end-to-end budget decomposed per hop with owners, hops re-sequenced — fraud checks parallelized, non-critical work made async with event sourcing, the critical path reduced to four hops — and load models rehearsed at 130% of forecast peak before the season. The budget holds; the reasons became events.
